facts.fact: The Portfolio Committee on Home Affairs reports that the Department's 2025/26 target of rolling out automated birth registration functionality to 47 health facilities was missed: development of the e-Birth system was not completed in Quarter 2, user acceptance testing was not signed off in Quarter 3, and the rollout was deferred to 2026/27 because the Electronic Travel Authorisation and the reinstatement of citizenship were given priority.

The Portfolio Committee on Home Affairs reports that by the end of Quarter 3 of 2025/26 the e-Birth system was still in development and unsigned at user acceptance testing, so automated birth registration functionality had reached none of the 47 health facilities targeted for the year; the report gives no count of facilities or offices registering births by any other digital means.

The Department of Home Affairs' Annual Performance Plan for 2025/26 carries an annual target to roll out automated birth registration functionality to 47 health facilities, with completion of e-Birth system development as its first-quarter milestone, as the Portfolio Committee reports it.

The e-Birth system is the Department of Home Affairs' own project, set as a target in its Annual Performance Plan for 2025/26 and signed off by its Deputy Director-General for Civic Services, as the Portfolio Committee reports it.

note: The report says it covers 1 April to 31 December 2026, a slip for 2025: it is Quarters 1 to 3 of 2025/26, presented on 17 February 2026. No events or made fact: the e-Birth system is not live, and the report does not say how or where a birth is entered today. The offices value of none is for the e-Birth system alone. Also stated: births registered within 30 days were 172,560, 175,285 and 158,070 in the three quarters; 180,025 births were registered in Quarter 1 in all.
